part.name: Tapered clevis-to-hook lever
part.description: A single-piece elongated lever with a two-lug clevis and transverse pivot bore at one end, a tapered load-carrying arm, and an open curved hook or catch interface at the opposite end.
part.symmetry_note: The part is substantially symmetric about the longitudinal mid-plane y=0. The two clevis lugs, split pivot bore, arm width, and hook are mirrored across this plane; the profile is not symmetric through the thickness direction z.

Section.name: Clevis pivot end
Section.function intent: Provides a pinned joint that locates a mating link or bracket between two lugs while allowing rotation about the transverse pin axis.
Section.physical behavior: The two lugs react pin shear and bearing loads on opposite sides of the central slot. Their separation stabilizes the mating member against lateral motion, while the rounded outer profiles distribute bearing and bending stress into the tapered arm.
Section.geometry: A forked end composed of two parallel rounded lugs separated by a rectangular slot. Coaxial cylindrical bore segments pass through the lugs, and the slot ends at a flat transverse wall toward the arm.
Section.location: At the broad negative-x end of the part; shown at the left in the front and isometric views.

major_faces.name: Negative-side lug outer arc
major_faces.description: Radius-7.5 cylindrical outer surface forming the rounded perimeter of the negative-y clevis lug.

major_faces.name: Negative-side slot wall
major_faces.description: Planar inner face of the negative-y lug, including the circular opening around the pivot bore.

major_faces.name: Clevis slot end wall
major_faces.description: Flat transverse wall at x=-60.75 that terminates the central clevis slot and joins both lugs to the arm.

major_faces.name: Positive-side slot wall
major_faces.description: Planar inner face of the positive-y lug, including the circular opening around the pivot bore.

major_faces.name: Positive-side lug outer arc
major_faces.description: Radius-7.5 cylindrical outer surface forming the rounded perimeter of the positive-y clevis lug.

major_faces.name: Positive-lug pivot bore
major_faces.description: Radius-3 cylindrical bore patch through the positive-y lug, coaxial with the opposite bore patch.

major_faces.name: Negative-lug pivot bore
major_faces.description: Radius-3 cylindrical bore patch through the negative-y lug, completing the transverse pin interface.

relationships.function relationship: constrains_dof; cooperates with the hook end to define the lever's two external interfaces

Section.name: Tapered lever arm
features included: load transition into both end interfaces
Section.function intent: Maintains the required separation between the pivot and hook interfaces and transmits tensile, compressive, bending, and torsional loads between them with reduced mass.
Section.physical behavior: The deep, gradually tapered solid section behaves as a beam. Its broad side faces resist in-plane bending, its top and bottom surfaces provide section depth, and the increasing width toward the clevis lowers stress near the more highly loaded pinned joint.
Section.geometry: A long solid prismatic arm whose width and thickness vary gradually along x. Four dominant planar patches form its top, bottom, and two side surfaces and continue into the unpartitioned end regions.
Section.location: Central portion of the part between the clevis pivot end and the hook end.

major_faces.name: Upper sloped arm face
major_faces.description: Large planar upper surface, slightly inclined along the arm and extending toward both end transitions.

major_faces.name: Negative-side arm face
major_faces.description: Large longitudinal planar side face on the negative-y side, including continuous coplanar regions at the ends.

major_faces.name: Lower sloped arm face
major_faces.description: Large planar lower surface with a slight longitudinal inclination and tapered outline.

major_faces.name: Positive-side arm face
major_faces.description: Large longitudinal planar side face on the positive-y side, mirrored from FACE 9.

Section.name: Hook catch end
Section.function intent: Engages a mating pin, edge, cable, or catch element through an open throat and retains it against the concave seat while allowing rapid lateral insertion or release.
Section.physical behavior: Contact load from the mating element is reacted by compression and bearing on the concave seat. The curved heel redirects this load into the arm, while the upright nose constrains escape in the hook-opening direction and the open throat supplies assembly clearance.
Section.geometry: A compact J-shaped end with a radius-3 concave seat, a larger radius-9 outer heel, a narrow upright cylindrical nose, and a planar top cap. Small planar and cylindrical transition patches resolve the intersections with the arm side faces.
Section.location: At the narrow positive-x end of the part; shown at the right in the front and isometric views.

major_faces.name: Hook concave seat
major_faces.description: Radius-3 cylindrical concave surface forming the principal mating and retention seat inside the hook.

major_faces.name: Upper throat transition
major_faces.description: Small radius-3 cylindrical transition surface at the upper side of the hook throat.

major_faces.name: Terminal nose cap
major_faces.description: Flat horizontal top face capping the upright hook nose.

major_faces.name: Terminal nose cylinder
major_faces.description: Vertical-axis radius-3 cylindrical outer surface forming the rounded free end of the hook nose.

major_faces.name: Hook outer heel
major_faces.description: Radius-9 cylindrical convex surface forming the lower outer heel and load-return path into the arm.

relationships.function relationship: locates_mating_part; forms the lever output interface relative to the pivot interface
